Namespace Tuinet.Testing

Classes

CellBufferTesting

Test assertions and dumps for a Tuinet.CellBuffer: a styled text format for snapshot files, ANSI for eyeballing in a terminal, and finding text on screen. Allocates freely: these are for tests, not frames.

ScreenAssertionException

A screen assertion failed: text missing from a buffer, or a buffer that doesn't match its snapshot.

Snapshot

Snapshot tests for frames: Tuinet.Testing.Snapshot.Verify(Tuinet.CellBuffer,System.String,System.Boolean,System.String,System.String) compares a buffer with snapshots/<name>.txt next to the test's source file. On a mismatch (or a missing snapshot) it writes <name>.received.txt beside it and throws; set TUINET_ACCEPT_SNAPSHOTS=1 to write the snapshots instead, then review them in the diff.

var buffer = new CellBuffer(40, 10);
app.Render(buffer, nowMs: 0);
Snapshot.Verify(buffer, "main-screen");
TestTerminal

Drives an Tuinet.IApp the way Tuinet.Terminal.Run(Tuinet.IApp,System.Int32) does, over a real Tuinet.Terminal on a Tuinet.Testing.TestTty, with a clock the test controls. It draws the first frame when created; after that each input call is one burst of events followed by one frame, as when a user acts and the loop catches up. Calls chain:

using var term = new TestTerminal(new MyApp(), 80, 24);
term.Press("jj").Key(KeyCode.Enter);
Assert.Contains("EDIT", term.Text);
term.Click("Save");

Typed calls (Tuinet.Testing.TestTerminal.Press(System.String), Tuinet.Testing.TestTerminal.Key(Tuinet.KeyCode,Tuinet.Modifiers), Tuinet.Testing.TestTerminal.Click(System.Int32,System.Int32,Tuinet.MouseButton)…) hand events straight to the app; Tuinet.Testing.TestTerminal.Input(System.String) sends raw bytes through the terminal's input parser.

TestTty

An in-memory Tuinet.ITty for tests: script input with Tuinet.Testing.TestTty.Enqueue(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte}), resize with Tuinet.Testing.TestTty.Resize(System.Int32,System.Int32), and inspect what the terminal wrote. Counts writes and bytes so tests can pin the output cost of a frame. Suspends are recorded instead of stopping the process, and Tuinet.Testing.TestTty.Signal(Tuinet.TtySignals) simulates job-control signals from outside.
